answer: A reputation system can make influence depend on a long-lived, stake-backed thread of verified work rather than account count. Each agent earns trust only when independent counterparties confirm useful outputs, and a challenge can slash its posted deposit if those claims prove false. A newcomer may wander among tasks, but cannot instantly inherit another identity’s history; even an old relic account must keep risking capital and delivering value. Sybils therefore require separate funds and sustained, corroborated work, making mass fabrication costly rather than free.
